findings.title: Relocating the active workspace commits and re-lists before the new folder's sync state is detected
findings.body:
For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` runs `relocateActive`, which commits the gate and calls `afterCommit` (`switch-transaction.ts:135-137`). `afterCommit` calls `broadcastLibraryChanged()` and `broadcastState()` (`workspaces/index.ts:524-529`), so the windows re-list the library from the new folder. `syncStates.refresh(current)` only runs afterwards, at line 755. Until it finishes, `SyncStates.of` sees that the path changed and falls back to the path rule (`sync-state.ts:26-29`). That rule only recognises `~/Library/CloudStorage` and similar locations. A Google Drive or iCloud folder that only the xattr check recognises (the case the earlier threads on `index.ts:770` describe) therefore counts as not synced for the whole re-list:
- `activeEvictionProbe()` returns null (line 369), so the re-list gets no eviction probe.
- `activeScratch()` and `syncedStagingFor()` return null (lines 375, 397), so a recording started in that window stages in `.kaipu/tmp/` inside the synced folder.
- `refresh` can take up to the 2 s detection timeout, which widens the window.

The add and create paths avoid this: they call `syncStates.refresh` before `runSwitch` (lines 578 and 630).

Fix: detect before the transaction commits. For example, call `syncStates.refresh({ id, path: chosen })` right before `relocateWorkspace` at line 751. If `outcome.ok` is false, re-run `syncStates.refresh(entry)` for the old entry, because the map would otherwise hold the chosen path under this id. Alternatively, do the refresh inside the `apply` callback so it runs before `gate.commit`.

contracts.action: After "Change folder…", detect the new folder's sync provider and return the refreshed workspace view
contracts.equivalent_path: addWorkspace and createWorkspace call syncStates.refresh right after the registry call and before runSwitch, then build the view with syncStates.of(entry)
contracts.before_after: Add and create: refresh runs before the switch commits, so the re-list sees the detected provider. Relocate: refresh runs after relocateWorkspace has already committed and fired afterCommit for the active workspace, so the re-list sees only the path rule.
contracts.visible_effect: The returned workspace view carries the detected sync provider and the bounded availability. For an xattr-only synced folder, the library re-list and capture staging right after the commit use the not-synced path.
contracts.failure_mode: syncStates.refresh goes through detectSync, which times out (2 s per the earlier thread) and returns null, leaving the path rule in charge until the next launch. A rejection from refresh would reject the IPC call after the relocation has already been persisted and committed. I did not read detectSync to confirm whether it can throw.
contracts.open_question: Does detectSync ever reject rather than resolve null? If it can, an unhandled rejection after the relocation is persisted would surface as a failed IPC call even though the folder was changed.

structuredOutput.summary: The 5-line change in `relocateFolder` adds a sync detection for the new folder and returns the refreshed workspace view. One problem: for the active workspace, the relocation commits and the windows re-list before `syncStates.refresh` runs, unlike add/create. A folder that only the xattr check recognises as synced is treated as not synced during that re-list. I raised one `fix` (medium confidence). None of the open threads sit on this file, so there are no thread replies.

findings.title: Relocating the active workspace commits and re-lists before the new folder's sync state is detected
findings.body:
For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` runs `relocateActive`, which commits the gate and calls `afterCommit` (`switch-transaction.ts:135-137`). `afterCommit` calls `broadcastLibraryChanged()` and `broadcastState()` (`workspaces/index.ts:524-529`), so the windows re-list the library from the new folder. `syncStates.refresh(current)` only runs afterwards, at line 755. Until it finishes, `SyncStates.of` sees that the path changed and falls back to the path rule (`sync-state.ts:26-29`). That rule only recognises `~/Library/CloudStorage` and similar locations. A Google Drive or iCloud folder that only the xattr check recognises (the case the earlier threads on `index.ts:770` describe) therefore counts as not synced for the whole re-list:
- `activeEvictionProbe()` returns null (line 369), so the re-list gets no eviction probe.
- `activeScratch()` and `syncedStagingFor()` return null (lines 375, 397), so a recording started in that window stages in `.kaipu/tmp/` inside the synced folder.
- `refresh` can take up to the 2 s detection timeout, which widens the window.

The add and create paths avoid this: they call `syncStates.refresh` before `runSwitch` (lines 578 and 630).

Fix: detect before the transaction commits. For example, call `syncStates.refresh({ id, path: chosen })` right before `relocateWorkspace` at line 751. If `outcome.ok` is false, re-run `syncStates.refresh(entry)` for the old entry, because the map would otherwise hold the chosen path under this id. Alternatively, do the refresh inside the `apply` callback so it runs before `gate.commit`.
